Key elements:
- Types have security annotations `kappa : security` with `reader` and `indirect_reader`.
- `flows_to l1 l2 = False` only when `l1 = High` and `l2 = Low`.
- Terms: unit, abs, app, pair, fst, snd, inl, inr, case, protect, if.
- Erasure `erase_security`.
- `same_result t1 t2 := forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> erase_security v1 = erase_security v2`.
- Theorem: two closed terms of same secret type in same typed context produce same erased results, provided result type ground and transparent and the secret's indirect reader can't flow to result's indirect reader.

This is a "termination-insensitive noninterference" via logical relation between two terms (a binary relation) at each type, parameterized by the "current label" (pc), and maybe a relation for the "same result" property.

The context lemma needs: for all C, if R_{T_secret}(t1,t2) then R_{T_result}(plug C t1, plug C t2). This is a "compatibility" property of the relation with the typing rules. For this to be provable compositionally, we need R to be defined compositionally in terms of types, and the typing rules involve subtyping and protection. E.g., for T_App: if R at Arrow T1 T2 kappa relates f1,f2 and R at T1 relates a1,a2, then R at ty_protect kappa.indirect T2 relates app f1 a1 r and app f2 a2 r. Let's think about how the "protect" mechanism works in the semantics: ST_AppAbs evaluates to `tm_protect kappa.indirect (open body v)`. And the type rule gives result `ty_protect kappa.indirect T2`. So the term-level protection corresponds to type-level protection. The `protect_value` at the term level only changes the security annotations of values: e.g., tm_unit kappa -> tm_unit (protect kappa l). Since erasure erases annotations, protection doesn't change erasure. But it matters for subsequent typing/relational reasoning: e.g., if we later take fst of a protected pair, the protection level matters.

Hmm, the term-level protection changes the value's security annotation, which then affects typing of the surrounding context (the context sees the protected type). E.g., `tm_fst (tm_protect l (pair v1 v2 kappa)) r`? Wait, the type rule T_Protect gives ty_protect l (Prod T1 T2 kappa) = Prod T1 T2 (protect kappa l). Semantically: step of protect: tm_protect l (pair ...) --> protect_value (pair v1 v2 kappa) l = pair v1 v2 (protect kappa l). Then fst steps: tm_fst (pair v1 v2 (protect kappa l)) r --> tm_protect (protect kappa l).indirect v1 (given flows_to (protect kappa l).reader r). So the value v1 gets protected at a higher level. In the erased semantics, this doesn't matter, but the type-level relation must be consistent.

So the value relation must satisfy: if v1 ~ v2 at T, then protect_value v1 l ~ protect_value v2 l at ty_protect l T (at whatever level parameter).

### Setting up a Kripke-ish relation

I think the natural relation here is exactly the standard one for noninterference in a language with a "protect" primitive:

Define, for a label l (the "observer level"/"protection level") and type T:
- `E l T t1 t2` : terms related.
- `V l T v1 v2` : values related.

- `V l (Unit kappa) v1 v2 := True` (since erased equality trivial; but maybe require `flows_to kappa.reader l -> erase v1 = erase v2`, which is also True).

Let's see: T_Inl gives type Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa' for the annotation kappa' on the term. To get type Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa, use T_Sub with S_Sum requiring security_le kappa' kappa. So the term's annotation may differ from the type's. So matching should be on constructors (inl/inr), not annotations. Good: erase discards annotations anyway.

```
Fixpoint V (p : label) (l : label) (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit kappa => fun v1 v2 => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa => fun v1 v2 =>
      let kap := protect_security kappa p in
      flows_to kap.indirect l ->
      (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\ V Low l T1 a1 a2)
      \/ (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr a2 k2 /\ V Low l T2 a1 a2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 kappa => fun v1 v2 =>
      let kap := protect_security kappa p in
      flows_to kap.indirect l ->
      exists a1 a2 b1 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ V Low l T1 a1 a2 /\ V Low l T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 kappa => fun f1 f2 =>
      let kap := protect_security kappa p in
      forall r, flows_to kap.reader r ->
        forall u1 u2, E Low l T1 u1 u2 ->
          E (join p kappa.indirect?) l (T2 with protection...) ...
  end
```

- `label` order: `le_label l1 l2 := flows_to l1 l2`. Reflexive, transitive.
- `V (p : label) (l : label) (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop`
- `E (p l : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) := forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> V p l T v1 v2`.

Definition:
```
V p l (Unit kappa) v1 v2 := True

Let me now write down the full definition of V concretely (with `value` included):

```coq
Fixpoint V (p : label) (l : label) (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit kappa => fun v1 v2 => value v1 /\ value v2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa => fun v1 v2 =>
      value v1 /\ value v2 /\
      (flows_to (protect_security kappa p).(indirect_reader) l ->
       (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\
          security_le k1 (protect_security kappa p) /\
          security_le k2 (protect_security kappa p) /\
          V Low l T1 a1 a2)
       \/ (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr a2 k2 /\ ... V Low l T2 a1 a2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 kappa => fun v1 v2 =>
      value v1 /\ value v2 /\
      (flows_to (protect_security kappa p).(indirect_reader) l ->
       exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
         security_le k1 (protect_security kappa p) /\ security_le k2 (...) /\
         V Low l T1 a1 a2 /\ V Low l T2 b1 b2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 kappa => fun f1 f2 =>
      value f1 /\ value f2 /\
      exists T1a body1 k1 T1b body2 k2,
        f1 = tm_abs T1a body1 k1 /\ f2 = tm_abs T1b body2 k2 /\
        security_le k1 (protect_security kappa p) /\
        security_le k2 (protect_security kappa p) /\
        (forall r, flows_to (protect_security kappa p).(reader) r ->
         forall u1 u2,
           (forall w1 w2, evaluates u1 w1 -> evaluates u2 w2 -> V Low l T1 w1 w2) ->
           forall w1 w2,
             evaluates (tm_app f1 u1 r) w1 ->
             evaluates (tm_app f2 u2 r) w2 ->
             V (protect_security kappa p).(indirect_reader) l T2 w1 w2)
  end.
```

### Label decidability / case analysis

Since labels have two constructors, `destruct l` works. For arbitrary label expressions like `join a b`, `destruct a; destruct b; simpl`. Automation: `intros; destruct l1, l2; simpl; tauto` etc.

Approach via "context typing" (CONTEXT LEMMA): The standard approach in these benchmark tasks, I believe, is:

1. Define logical relation `interp l T t1 t2` (possibly split into value relation and term relation) where `l` is a label (observer level).
2. Fundamental theorem: for any context Gamma1/Gamma2 related environment, `has_type Gamma1 t T` and `has_type Gamma2 t T`? Hmm, same t or different t? For the target we need different t1, t2 with same type in empty context. So relation on two terms typed in two contexts that are related.

Since both terms have the same *surface* type T (not just subtype), we can require: for all x T1 T2, lookup x Gamma1 = Some T1 -> lookup x Gamma2 = Some T2 -> ... relation between substituted values at types T1 and T2? Standard: substitutions rho1, rho2 with `interp l T1 (rho1 x) (rho2 x)` when lookups give T1 and T2 with T1, T2 related somehow. To keep it simple, since in the target both contexts are `update empty x T_secret` — identical — we can define env relation requiring both lookups return the same type T and terms rho1 x ~_l^T rho2 x.

But for the fundamental theorem we need to handle T_Sub, which changes types to subtypes. Then Gamma1 and Gamma2 lookups give types T1, T2 that may differ but are related by subtyping. Now, the **fundamental theorem statement**. Let me write it carefully.

I need a substitution operation for envs. Options:
(a) Simultaneous substitution `subst_rho : (atom -> tm) -> tm -> tm`.
(b) Use the existing `subst` repeatedly for a finite env. Since contexts are lists, could define substitution of a list of (atom, tm) pairs. Simultaneous is cleaner.

Let me define:
```
Fixpoint subst_rho (rho : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => rho x
  | tm_unit k => tm_unit k
  | tm_abs T body k => tm_abs T (subst_rho rho body) k
  | ...
  end.
```
Note: same as subst but replacing all fvars.

Hmm, wait: Vp l j T is the relation at ty_protect j T. Its invariant should be k_v ⊑ security_of(T) ⊔ j, i.e., security_le k_v (protect_security (security_of T) j). Let me define Vp accordingly:

```
Fixpoint Vp (l j : label) (T : ty) (x y : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      if flows_to (join k.ind j) l then
        exists kv1 kv2,
          security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
          security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
          ((exists u1 u2, x = tm_inl u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inl u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T1 u1 u2)
           \/ (exists u1 u2, x = tm_inr u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inr u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T2 u1 u2))
      else True
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k => similar (security_le on kv) with pairs and both components
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      if flows_to (join k.ind j) l then
        exists kv1 kv2, security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\ security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
          forall w1 w2 r, flows_to (join k.reader j) r -> Vp l Low T1 w1 w2 ->
            forall u1 u2, evaluates (tm_app x w1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app y w2 r) u2 ->
              Vp l (join k.ind j) T2 u1 u2
      else True
  end.
```

Let me now define Vp precisely.

```
Definition vis l jk := flows_to jk l.   (* jk is the joined indirect level *)
```

```
Fixpoint Vp (l : label) (j : label) (T : ty) (x y : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  value x /\ value y /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k =>
      if flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l
      then exists kv1 kv2 : security, x = tm_unit kv1 /\ y = tm_unit kv2
      else True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      if flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l
      then exists kv1 kv2 : security,
             security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
             security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
             ((exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inl u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inl u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T1 u1 u2)
              \/ (exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inr u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inr u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T2 u1 u2))
      else True
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      if flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l
      then exists kv1 kv2 : security,
             security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
             security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
             (exists a1 b1 a2 b2 : tm,
                x = tm_pair a1 b1 kv1 /\ y = tm_pair a2 b2 kv2 /\
                Vp l Low T1 a1 a2 /\ Vp l Low T2 b1 b2)
      else True
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      if flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l
      then exists kv1 kv2 : security,
             security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
             security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
             (exists T1x bodyx T1y bodyy : ty? ...)
             ...
      else True
  end
```

(D) `E_protect : E l j T e1 e2 -> E l (join j j') T (tm_protect j' e1) (tm_protect j' e2)` (via multi_protect_inv + A2).

Definition Vp (l j : label) (T : ty) (x y : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with

      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists kv1 kv2, x = tm_unit kv1 /\ y = tm_unit kv2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>

                      security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
                      ((exists u1 u2, x = tm_inl u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inl u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T1 u1 u2)

  ...
```

Let me now write the definition concretely, with the exact field projections to help reduction. I'll use `kappa.(indirect_reader)` etc.

```
Fixpoint Vp (l j : label) (T : ty) (x y : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists kv1 kv2 : security, x = tm_unit kv1 /\ y = tm_unit kv2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists kv1 kv2 : security,
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        ((exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inl u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inl u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T1 u1 u2)
         \/ (exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inr u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inr u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T2 u1 u2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists kv1 kv2 : security,
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        (exists a1 b1 a2 b2 : tm,
            x = tm_pair a1 b1 kv1 /\ y = tm_pair a2 b2 kv2 /\
            Vp l Low T1 a1 a2 /\ Vp l Low T2 b1 b2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists (T1x T1y : ty) (bodyx bodyy : tm) (kv1 kv2 : security),
        x = tm_abs T1x bodyx kv1 /\ y = tm_abs T1y bodyy kv2 /\
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        (forall (w1 w2 : tm) (r : label),
            value w1 -> value w2 -> flows_to (join k.(reader) j) r ->
            Vp l Low T1 w1 w2 ->
            forall u1 u2 : tm,
              evaluates (tm_app x w1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app y w2 r) u2 ->
              Vp l (join k.(indirect_reader) j) T2 u1 u2)
  end.
```
Note `Vp` is a Fixpoint returning Prop; the recursive calls are on T1, T2 with different j/l — structural on T ✓ (Coq accepts since Ty_Sum T1 T2 k has T1, T2 as subterms; the match is on T and recursive calls on T1/T2 ✓).

But wait: the arrow case's recursive call `Vp l (join k.ind j) T2` — T2 is a subterm ✓. And `Vp l Low T1` ✓.

Then E:
```
Definition E (l j : label) (T : ty) (e1 e2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates e1 v1 -> evaluates e2 v2 -> Vp l j T v1 v2.
```

Definition env_rel (l : label) (Gamma : context) (rho1 rho2 : atom -> tm) : Prop :=

```

  multi s u -> value u ->

      * right. exists v, k. split; [eapply multi_step; eauto | split; [exact Hv' | split; [exact Hflow | exists w; split; [exact Hmw | split; [exact Hvw | exact Hu]]]]].

**subst_rho**:
```
Fixpoint subst_rho (rho : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => rho x
  | tm_unit k => tm_unit k
  | tm_abs T body k => tm_abs T (subst_rho rho body) k
  | tm_app t1 t2 r => tm_app (subst_rho rho t1) (subst_rho rho t2) r
  | tm_pair t1 t2 k => tm_pair (subst_rho rho t1) (subst_rho rho t2) k
  | tm_fst t1 r => tm_fst (subst_rho rho t1) r
  | tm_snd t1 r => tm_snd (subst_rho rho t1) r
  | tm_inl t1 k => tm_inl (subst_rho rho t1) k
  | tm_inr t1 k => tm_inr (subst_rho rho t1) k
  | tm_case t0 b1 b2 r => tm_case (subst_rho rho t0) (subst_rho rho b1) (subst_rho rho b2) r
  | tm_protect l t1 => tm_protect l (subst_rho rho t1)
  | tm_if c y n r => tm_if (subst_rho rho c) (subst_rho rho y) (subst_rho rho n) r
  end.
```

  | x :: L' => Nat.max x (max_list L')

Lemma max_list_spec : forall L x, In x L -> x <= max_list L.

  - inversion Hx.

**context_fv and subst_rho_plug**: Let me define context_fv:
```
Fixpoint context_fv (C : program_context) : list atom :=
  match C with
  | C_Hole => []
  | C_Abs T C' k => context_fv C'
  | C_AppLeft C' t2 r => context_fv C' ++ fv t2
  | C_AppRight t1 C' r => fv t1 ++ context_fv C'
  | C_PairLeft C' t2 k => context_fv C' ++ fv t2
  | C_PairRight t1 C' k => fv t1 ++ context_fv C'
  | C_Fst C' r => context_fv C'
  | C_Snd C' r => context_fv C'
  | C_Inl C' k => context_fv C'
  | C_Inr C' k => context_fv C'
  | C_CaseScrutinee C' b1 b2 r => context_fv C' ++ fv b1 ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseLeft t0 C' b2 r => fv t0 ++ context_fv C' ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseRight t0 b1 C' r => fv t0 ++ fv b1 ++ context_fv C'
  | C_Protect l C' => context_fv C'
  | C_IfCondition C' y n r => context_fv C' ++ fv y ++ fv n
  | C_IfThen c C' n r => fv c ++ context_fv C' ++ fv n
  | C_IfElse c y C' r => fv c ++ fv y ++ context_fv C'
  end.
```

**context_fv + plug lemma**. Let me write context_fv in the plug constructor order:
C_Hole, C_Abs, C_AppLeft, C_AppRight, C_PairLeft, C_PairRight, C_Fst, C_Snd, C_Inl, C_Inr, C_CaseScrutinee, C_CaseLeft, C_CaseRight, C_Protect, C_IfCondition, C_IfThen, C_IfElse.

```
Fixpoint context_fv (C : program_context) : list atom :=
  match C with
  | C_Hole => []
  | C_Abs T C' k => context_fv C'
  | C_AppLeft C' t2 r => context_fv C' ++ fv t2
  | C_AppRight t1 C' r => fv t1 ++ context_fv C'
  | C_PairLeft C' t2 k => context_fv C' ++ fv t2
  | C_PairRight t1 C' k => fv t1 ++ context_fv C'
  | C_Fst C' r => context_fv C'
  | C_Snd C' r => context_fv C'
  | C_Inl C' k => context_fv C'
  | C_Inr C' k => context_fv C'
  | C_CaseScrutinee C' b1 b2 r => context_fv C' ++ fv b1 ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseLeft t0 C' b2 r => fv t0 ++ context_fv C' ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseRight t0 b1 C' r => fv t0 ++ fv b1 ++ context_fv C'
  | C_Protect l C' => context_fv C'
  | C_IfCondition C' y n r => context_fv C' ++ fv y ++ fv n
  | C_IfThen c C' n r => fv c ++ context_fv C' ++ fv n
  | C_IfElse c y C' r => fv c ++ fv y ++ context_fv C'
  end.
```

Lemma subst_rho_plug : forall C x u,
  ~ In x (context_fv C) ->
  subst_rho (extend_rho id_rho x u) (plug C (tm_fvar x)) = plug C u.
Proof.
  induction C as [| T C' k IHC | C' t2 r IHC | t1 C' r IHC | C' t2 k IHC | t1 C' k IHC
                 | C' r IHC | C' r IHC | C' k IHC | C' k IHC
                 | C' b1 b2 r IHC | t0 C' b2 r IHC | t0 b1 C' r IHC | l C' IHC
                 | C' y n r IHC | c C' n r IHC | c y C' r IHC];
    intros x u Hx; simpl in *.
```
Wait, the induction pattern: program_context constructors and their arguments:
- C_Hole: no args.
- C_Abs : ty -> program_context -> security -> program_context: args T, C' (recursive), k.
- C_AppLeft : program_context -> tm -> label: C', t2, r.
- C_AppRight : tm -> program_context -> label: t1, C', r.
- C_PairLeft : program_context -> tm -> security.
- C_PairRight : tm -> program_context -> security.
- C_Fst : program_context -> label.
- C_Snd : program_context -> label.
- C_Inl : program_context -> security.
- C_Inr : program_context -> security.
- C_CaseScrutinee : program_context -> tm -> tm -> label.
- C_CaseLeft : tm -> program_context -> tm -> label.
- C_CaseRight : tm -> tm -> program_context -> label.
- C_Protect : label -> program_context.
- C_IfCondition : program_context -> tm -> tm -> label.
- C_IfThen : tm -> program_context -> tm -> label.
- C_IfElse : tm -> tm -> program_context -> label.
The `as` patterns for induction on program_context: for each constructor, list args in order with IH after the recursive one:
- C_Hole: []
- C_Abs: [T C' IHC k]
- C_AppLeft: [C' IHC t2 r]
- C_AppRight: [t1 C' IHC r]
- C_PairLeft: [C' IHC t2 k]
- C_PairRight: [t1 C' IHC k]
- C_Fst: [C' IHC r]
- C_Snd: [C' IHC r]
- C_Inl: [C' IHC k]
- C_Inr: [C' IHC k]
- C_CaseScrutinee: [C' IHC b1 b2 r]
- C_CaseLeft: [t0 C' IHC b2 r]
- C_CaseRight: [t0 b1 C' IHC r]
- C_Protect: [l C' IHC] (note label first)
- C_IfCondition: [C' IHC y n r]
- C_IfThen: [c C' IHC n r]
- C_IfElse: [c y C' IHC r]

Now each case proof after `intros x u Hx; simpl in *`:

```coq
Fixpoint Vp (l j : label) (T : ty) (x y : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists kv1 kv2 : security, x = tm_unit kv1 /\ y = tm_unit kv2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists kv1 kv2 : security,
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        ((exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inl u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inl u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T1 u1 u2)
         \/ (exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inr u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inr u2 kv2 /\ Vp l Low T2 u1 u2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists kv1 kv2 : security,
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        (exists a1 b1 a2 b2 : tm,
            x = tm_pair a1 b1 kv1 /\ y = tm_pair a2 b2 kv2 /\
            Vp l Low T1 a1 a2 /\ Vp l Low T2 b1 b2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) j) l ->
      exists (T1x T1y : ty) (bodyx bodyy : tm) (kv1 kv2 : security),
        x = tm_abs T1x bodyx kv1 /\ y = tm_abs T1y bodyy kv2 /\
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        (forall (w1 w2 : tm) (r : label),
            value w1 -> value w2 -> flows_to (join k.(reader) j) r ->
            Vp l Low T1 w1 w2 ->
            forall u1 u2 : tm,
              evaluates (tm_app x w1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app y w2 r) u2 ->
              Vp l (join k.(indirect_reader) j) T2 u1 u2)
  end.
```

Lemma Vp_protect : forall T l j j1 j2 x y,
  Vp l j T x y ->

    destruct (H ltac:(eapply flows_to_trans; [apply flows_to_join_r_mono; apply flows_to_trans with (b := join j j1); [apply flows_to_join_ab | apply flows_to_join_ab] | exact Hvis]))

```coq
Fixpoint VpS (l j : label) (T : ty) (x y : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k => exists kv1 kv2 : security, x = tm_unit kv1 /\ y = tm_unit kv2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      exists kv1 kv2 : security,
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        ((exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inl u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inl u2 kv2 /\
             (flows_to (join (security_of T1).(indirect_reader) Low) l -> VpS l Low T1 u1 u2))
         \/ (exists u1 u2 : tm, x = tm_inr u1 kv1 /\ y = tm_inr u2 kv2 /\
             (flows_to (join (security_of T2).(indirect_reader) Low) l -> VpS l Low T2 u1 u2)))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      exists kv1 kv2 : security,
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        (exists a1 b1 a2 b2 : tm,
            x = tm_pair a1 b1 kv1 /\ y = tm_pair a2 b2 kv2 /\
            (flows_to (join (security_of T1).(indirect_reader) Low) l -> VpS l Low T1 a1 a2) /\
            (flows_to (join (security_of T2).(indirect_reader) Low) l -> VpS l Low T2 b1 b2))
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      exists (T1x T1y : ty) (bodyx bodyy : tm) (kv1 kv2 : security),
        x = tm_abs T1x bodyx kv1 /\ y = tm_abs T1y bodyy kv2 /\
        security_le kv1 (protect_security k j) /\
        security_le kv2 (protect_security k j) /\
        (forall (w1 w2 : tm) (r : label),
            value w1 -> value w2 -> flows_to (join k.(reader) j) r ->
            (flows_to (join (security_of T1).(indirect_reader) Low) l -> VpS l Low T1 w1 w2) ->
            forall u1 u2 : tm,
              evaluates (tm_app x w1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app y w2 r) u2 ->
              (flows_to (join (security_of T2).(indirect_reader) (join k.(indirect_reader) j)) l ->
               VpS l (join k.(indirect_reader) j) T2 u1 u2))
  end.

Definition Vp (l j : label) (T : ty) (x y : tm) : Prop :=
  flows_to (join (security_of T).(indirect_reader) j) l -> VpS l j T x y.
```
